analysis.title: GS Financials & REITs Sector Specialist: Midday update / inbounds
key_insights: Defensives are in favor on 10 Nov 2026. P&C insurance carriers see the greatest tailwind, helped by rates. Brokers, card networks, exchanges and senior housing REITs are all up 1-2% as of send. The desk says this is not a blanket underperformance of offensives, because rates and travel help some pockets.

After the CPI print, mortgage names sharply underperform (RKT -6%, COMP -6%). REITs underperform, with Office REITs and Brokers down 2-4%, and BX lags peers in alternative asset managers. Wealth and Life insurance outperform.
Regional banks show dispersion: FCNCA and ZION are up strongly while WAL is down sharply.

Consumer REITs (lodging, malls, strip centers) outperform the index by 1-2%. Financials are more mixed: AXP slightly outperforms, while discretionary payments names lag (TOST, FOUR). The desk asks whether firm travel spend and good hotel data are making the consumer look like an inflation beneficiary.

Datacenters are heavily discussed in other sectors, particularly industrials (per Novak). Beneficiaries such as GEV are down by a mid-single-digit percent, and industrial investors are asking about ripple effects. Financials are quiet: AI capex beneficiaries in alternatives trade fine and some outperform, and datacenter REITs are flat. Specialists often call the datacenter REIT sympathy trading with broader datacenter development sentiment wrong.
FDS: feedback over the day has tilted slightly less negative. Positive engagement KPIs in the presentation suggest targets are more of a floor and set FDS up as a potential beat-and-raise story.

AMG was the most-asked-about stock on the capital markets zoom. The stock is up 5% on T+1 after earnings. Investor focus is on the growth trajectory, capital return and the regulatory backdrop after the election.
LINE reported disappointing earnings. Investors are asking why the print diverged from expectations built on peer earnings and USDA data.

MRX: GIR (Blostein) has greater conviction in the durability of earnings growth into 2027, even with more normalized trading volumes than 2026. Management is confident in 10%-20% PBT growth next year against tough comps. Prime balances are resilient and management points to market share gains despite pressure across levered ETFs. PBT margin reached 24% in 3Q vs 21% in 2025, with a path to 30% over time. Four M&A deals have terms largely agreed.

ZION: GIR (Nash) sees management confidence and conservatism on the levers behind its +8-12% NII guide, which some investors doubt. The deposit beta guide is conservative and assumes $1.5bn of DDA migration. Fixed-rate repricing comes from $550mn of quarterly securities repricing and $1.5bn of loans. Nash's analysis gets to +9.5% if the rate backdrop holds. Low securities yields could add 40-50bps to NIM over time. Capital return should rise in 2027 with Basel a ~90bp benefit.
SYF monthly results were solid: delinquencies in line, net charge-offs and loan growth better than seasonality. DQs rose 10bps MoM to 4.4% vs seasonal +9bps. NCOs were flat MoM vs seasonal +25bps.

SYF October monthly (reported): DQs +10bps MoM to 4.4% vs seasonal +9bps, and -10bps YoY. NCOs flat MoM vs seasonal +25bps, and -70bps YoY. Cycle-adjusted NCOs were 18bps per day vs 16bps the prior month. End-of-period loans +40bps MoM vs seasonal flat, and average loans +30bps MoM vs seasonal -70bps.
